R-112-23 through R-112-26 depend on spec 108's corpus:read grant model. CORRECTED 2026-08-20: spec 108 is 'blocked', NOT 'specs_hardened' as this finding previously asserted, and it still targets the same 'next' train. Its grant model is BUILT, MOUNTED AND GREEN — SCOPE-01 (scope registration), SCOPE-02 (observe-stage plumbing), SCOPE-03 (gate mount) and SCOPE-05 (docs, release train, flag bundles) are all Done, and 87 of its 90 DoD items are closed with executed evidence. What remains is SCOPE-04 (caller remediation), Blocked on three operator-owned, time-bound items no code can satisfy: a >= 14-day OBSERVE window, proactive rotation of principals whose grants are unknowable, and a go/no-go query returning an empty or explicitly-accepted denial set. The gate therefore runs in the OBSERVE (non-denying) stage and its enforcement flip is gated by a daily review carrying blocks_on_failure: [release-train-promote]. Surfacing capabilities before that boundary actually DENIES still violates policy P4 (reach never outruns the guard), so SCOPE-03 and everything downstream of it still cannot execute first.
outstandingFindings.correctionNote: THIS FINDING'S RATIONALE IS MATERIALLY WEAKER AFTER THE CORRECTION, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN USED TO SILENTLY DOWNGRADE IT. The original rationale was 'the grant model does not exist yet'. The real rationale is 'the grant model exists, is mounted and is green, but does not yet deny'. The blocking flag is deliberately LEFT AT true and the severity LEFT AT BLOCKING, because P4 is about enforcement and an observing gate does not enforce. Whether that residual gap still warrants BLOCKING rather than HIGH is a judgement for bubbles.plan as the routed owner; a fact correction is not a licence to reclassify.

outstandingFindings.summary: The registry's unit is the capability; the built artifacts are prompt contracts, and the mapping is not 1:1 — 17 of 27 contracts carry a routable id, 10 are pipeline stages that carry none. The rule that decides what constitutes one capability, and how contracts bind to capabilities, is undecided. Getting it wrong reproduces the original duplication at a new granularity.

R-112-31 requires the coverage check to compare against an independently derived universe of built capabilities. How that universe is derived — and how it avoids the circularity already present at tests/integration/experience/route_inventory_test.go:92-100, where the expected set is built from the catalog under validation — is undecided. Without this the check cannot fail and is decorative.

Spec 109 explicitly forbids deriving the MCP tool list by passthrough from agent.All(). The external tool projection must therefore be a per-capability declared projection, not a blanket export of the capability set. Reconciling R-112-08 with that constraint is a design decision.

Three navigation authorities are live and already divergent, and internal/experience/catalog.go:10 records that their cutover was deferred to a later scope of the shell specification. Whether this feature performs that cutover or hands it to the shell spec is undecided, and R-112-09 cannot be satisfied by whichever spec does not.

The slash alias table and the assistant registry currently contradict each other on /ask, /recipe and /cook. Generating both from one descriptor forces a decision about which existing behaviour is correct. That decision changes shipped user-visible behaviour for at least one token and cannot be made silently by a generator.

29 of 31 first-party PWA pages render no shared navigation. R-112-20 is satisfiable in principle by a core that reaches only surfaces which render navigation at all, which would make the guarantee vacuous on most pages. The relationship between this feature's guarantee and the island pages must be stated rather than assumed.

The authoring brief noted that .specify/templates/spec-template.md is expected to govern spec structure; that file does not exist in this repository (.specify/ contains only memory/, metrics/ and runtime/). spec.md follows the adjacent sibling spec's structure and the Bubbles BDD scenario contract instead. Either the template should be installed or the instruction corrected.

TWO FACTS WERE FOUND THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT STATE, BOTH STRENGTHENING IT. First, the capability reference already exists and points at nothing: every catalog surface carries a capability_id and validator.go:99 already emits an unknown-capability violation, but no capability record exists anywhere — in config/smackerel.yaml capability_id appears only as a surface attribute (:2706-2934) with no capabilities: block, and the only production-shaped test supplies the universe via iCapsOf(cat) at tests/integration/experience/route_inventory_test.go:92-100, deriving the expected set from the catalog under validation so the check is circular and cannot fail. Second, the predicted drift is already real and was demonstrated with three live contradictions: web/pwa/lib/appnav.js:22 asserts it mirrors internal/web/appshell.go:31 but the two have diverged (capture/connectors/photos PWA-only, knowledge server-only); internal/assistant/shortcuts.go:47 maps /ask to open_knowledge while config/assistant/scenarios.yaml:25-31 assigns /ask to retrieval_qa; and shortcuts.go:50-51 ships /recipe and /cook while scenarios.yaml records recipe_search with an empty shortcut and a comment that the set is frozen without them.
executionHistory.claimSharpened: THE BRIEF'S FIGURE OF 22 UNSURFACED CAPABILITIES WAS NARROWED TO 11 ON EVIDENCE, NOT ACCEPTED AS GIVEN. D17 and the plan of record both reach 22 as 27 minus 5; the arithmetic is correct but the units are mixed, because a prompt contract is not a capability. Ten of the 27 contracts declare a pipeline type (domain-extraction x3, query-augment, lint-audit, ingest-synthesis, drive-folder-context, drive-classification, digest-assembly, cross-source-connection) and carry no routable id: at all — they are invoked directly by their owning service and were never dispatchable. One more, e2e_ollama_smoke, is a test harness by its own description. Only the 17 contracts declaring type: scenario carry a routable id. The genuinely unsurfaced dispatchable set is therefore 11: alert_timing_evaluate, annotation_classify, expertise_classify, hospitality_concern_evaluate, recommendation_feedback, recommendation_reactive, recommendation_watch_evaluate, recommendation_why, relationship_cooling_evaluate, resurface_evaluate, retrieval_evergreen. This narrows the count and strengthens the finding: the real defect is that the repository cannot tell you which number is right, because nothing records whether a contract is unsurfaced deliberately or by omission. D18 was likewise held to its stated scope — a core-membership finding, not an unreachability claim — because internal/web/templates.go:79-84 appends the digest link after including the shared partial, so the digest IS reachable in the server shell while absent from the shared core.

executionHistory.releaseTrainRationale: Chose 'next' (target_slot staging) over 'mvp' (target_slot prod) on four grounds. (1) This feature RAISES REACH while the guard that should bound it is not delivered: surfacing the eleven currently-undeclared dispatchable capabilities makes them invocable by anyone who can talk to the assistant, and the per-capability authorization that bounds that — spec 108's corpus:read — is specs_hardened, not delivered, and targets 'next'. Shipping the exposure on the live train while its boundary lives on the other train is exactly what policy P4 forbids. (2) Both hard dependencies are on 'next': spec 108 (grants) and spec 109 (external tool surface) are both specs_hardened there, so a registry on 'mvp' would project into a tool list that does not exist on that train and declare grants that train does not enforce. (3) It replaces three live and already-divergent navigation authorities on a running shell, which is a change with real regression surface on every page a user touches; proving it on staging first is the correct order. (4) The sibling precedent is consistent — spec 111 chose 'next' on the same reasoning, and spec 108 states in its own words that a security-posture change MUST NOT ship on mvp. The honest cost of this choice — that the mvp train keeps the D17/D18 reachability gap for longer — is stated explicitly in spec.md rather than obscured by the train choice.

executionHistory.g094ShapeRationale: Answered G094 DIFFERENTLY from sibling spec 111, and deliberately so. Spec 111 took the proportionate Single-Capability / Single-Implementation branch because it has one implementation. Spec 112 takes the HEAVY foundation shape, because a capability registry genuinely IS a reusable foundation with real variation: spec.md §4.1 already defines Projection as a primitive, §4.2 already states that every ReachabilitySurface is a Projection of the descriptor set, and four concrete projections (assistant intent, navigation core, alias, external tool) are already enumerated with their own scopes and their own gating findings. Forcing the cheaper branch here would have been the premature-abstraction inverse: understating a foundation that the requirements already establish, in order to satisfy a gate more easily.
